title: Ball in Tyre Tracks on Fairway
question: Your tee shot finishes in deep tyre tracks left by a maintenance vehicle in the fairway. Can you take free relief?

choices.text: Yes. Tyre tracks are always ground under repair.
Yes. Any damage caused by greenkeeping equipment qualifies for free relief.
No. Unless the tyre tracks have been marked as Ground Under Repair or the Committee has declared them to be an abnormal course condition, you must play the ball as it lies.
Yes, but only if the tyre tracks are deep.

explanation: Tyre tracks do not automatically entitle a player to free relief. Relief is only available if the Committee has marked the area as Ground Under Repair (GUR) or has otherwise declared it to be an abnormal course condition under Rule 16.1. If not, the ball must be played as it lies, or relief may be taken under another rule (such as unplayable ball, with penalty). Many golfers mistakenly believe any course machinery damage qualifies for free relief, but this is not the case.
